open Metric InnerProductSpace
open scoped Manifold InnerProductSpace
variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
definition_context: E →L[ℝ] E is the space of real continuous linear endomorphisms. A.IsSymmetric means ⟨A u,v⟩=⟨u,A v⟩ for all u,v.
sphere (0:E) 1 is the subtype of unit-norm ambient vectors. The orthogonal complement (ℝ ∙ x)ᗮ is an ambient-vector subtype; coercion forgets its membership proof.
𝓡 n is the standard real smooth-manifold model for the n-dimensional unit sphere in an ambient space of dimension n+1. TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x is its tangent fiber.

mvfderiv is Mathlib's manifold differential, totalized to zero outside differentiability. The coercion from the sphere into E is the literal inclusion, and the displayed inner product is the ambient real inner product.
Fact P is a typeclass packaging a proof of proposition P; Module.finrank ℝ E is the finite real dimension.
cases.statement:
example
    (n : ℕ) [Fact (Module.finrank ℝ E = n + 1)]
    (A : E →L[ℝ] E) (hA : A.IsSymmetric) (x : sphere (0 : E) 1) :
    ∀ z : (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ,
      ((∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
        mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => ⟪(y : E), A (y : E)⟫_ℝ) x w =
          ⟪mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : sphere (0 : E) 1 → E) x w, (z : E)⟫_ℝ) ↔
        (z : E) = (2 : ℝ) • (A (x : E) - ⟪(x : E), A (x : E)⟫_ℝ • (x : E)))

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set Finset
open scoped ProbabilityTheory BigOperators
definition_context: Kernel A B assigns a measure on B measurably to each input in A. IsMarkovKernel means every such output measure has total mass one.
For any measure η, η.real t means (η t).toReal in Mathlib. ENNReal.toReal is totalized, with infinity sent to zero; probability assumptions give finite event masses in the displayed statement.
K ∘ₘ μ is the measure obtained by drawing an input with law μ and then using kernel K.
Integrable ε μ is real Bochner integrability, including almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the norm.

The binder ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ s, MeasurableSet s → ... asserts one common input null-set exception outside which the bound holds for every measurable event; it is not written with separate exceptional sets chosen after each event.
cases.statement:
example
    {A B : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B]
    (μ : Measure A) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (K L : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel K] [IsMarkovKernel L]
    (ε : A → ℝ) (hε : Integrable ε μ)
    (hbound : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ s, MeasurableSet s →
      |(K x).real s - (L x).real s| ≤ ε x) :
    ∀ t, MeasurableSet t →
      |(K ∘ₘ μ).real t - (L ∘ₘ μ).real t| ≤ ∫ x, ε x ∂μ
